10351: \begin{equation}

findings.finding: G_NEWTON is a dimensional input. The source repeatedly calls it measured physical input, not derived; matching the geometric coefficient to8piG is a normalization selection. This is positive evidence for the measured-G role, not a separately defined bare-G parameter.

The written coefficient is f0=1/(2kappa²)=c^4/(16piG). The same displayed G is not separately designated bare or laboratory-renormalized in this paragraph. A distinction required by a candidate background must therefore be introduced and calibrated explicitly; it is not supplied by a change of symbol.

findings.status: [DECLARADO] source claim, not a measured matching of the new branch
findings.finding: Matter is said to preserve standard minimal coupling in the bulk; inertial and gravitational mass equality is claimed as modular duality. This does not give the branch-specific conversion rho_eff/rho_inertial, nor equate optical lens mass with a dynamical GR-inferred mass in the presence of q.

The source withdraws the earlier G→G(1−beta) interpretation and the shifted Chandrasekhar-mass validation. It distinguishes the modular boundary from a universal local modification of G. This withdrawal supersedes using the earlier synthesis as a laboratory calibration law. The cited experimental arguments in the withdrawal were not re-audited here.

Ponte uses8piG in the conditional geometric equation and calls c,G conversion constants. These passages do not construct Cavendish matching for a nonzero background a or state a Jordan-to-laboratory response formula.

No explicit laboratory-background/Cavendish calibration of f0 against measured G_N, nor a relation fixing a_lab and rho_eff/rho_inertial, was located in this bounded search. No general absence in all archives is asserted. Historical luz supplied no matching equation under the targeted terms.

conditional_calibration_identity.status: [DERIVED] consequence of R15, not a recovered canonical law
conditional_calibration_identity.assumptions: c=1; static weak branch R15; compact nonrelativistic laboratory source; rho_eff=s_lab*rho_inertial with constant s_lab; q_lab constant; measured G_N defined from slow test-body acceleration for independently known inertial source mass.
conditional_calibration_identity.consequence: If one simultaneously identifies f0=1/(16pi G_N) AND s_lab=1, consistency requires q_lab=0. This is a consistency condition on those simultaneous identifications, not proof that a_lab=0 in the theory. A nonzero q_lab instead requires a justified matching of f0 and/or source normalization. Weak equivalence of test masses alone does not determine either.
conditional_calibration_identity.optical_comparison: For the same assumptions and a constant source normalization s_lens, optical coefficient relative to measured G_N is s_lens/[s_lab*(1+q_lab)]. For dynamical calibration within the lens, the optical-to-slow response ratio is1/(1+q_lens), only if both probe the same effective source profile and nuisance calibrations are controlled. These ratios do not select q, mass profiles or observed calibration errors.
